# TypeScript idiom

Match the repository's TypeScript version, module/runtime target, package manager, lint config, and
test stack. UI architecture and accessibility remain with `frontend-craft`.

## Types and boundaries

- Keep `strict` unless the existing migration plan says otherwise. Narrow `unknown` with runtime
  validation/type guards; avoid `any` crossing a public or trust boundary.
- Use discriminated unions for variants and an exhaustive `never` check. Separate caller input from
  server-owned output instead of making one reused interface incorrectly optional.
- Branded/opaque identifiers help only when same-primitive IDs are commonly confused; do not wrap
  every scalar by ritual.
- Module-scope state is process-wide. Keep request/user state in explicit context/arguments and make
  shared caches deliberately keyed, bounded, and concurrency-safe.

## Async and effects

- Every promise is awaited, returned, caught, or deliberately supervised. When the repository uses
  typescript-eslint, enable `@typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises` with type-aware linting; this is
  not a TypeScript compiler option. `void promise` may express intentional discard to the linter but
  does not handle rejection.
- Start independent work together only when concurrency is safe. Pass `AbortSignal`/cancellation and
  finite time budgets through client layers; ignore stale results after ownership changes.
- A failed response after a write is an unknown outcome. Retry only with the same server-enforced
  idempotency key and operation identity. Do not optimistically mutate destructive or money-moving
  actions without a real recovery contract.

## Verification

Use the repository's unit/component/network/browser tools; Vitest/Jest, Testing Library, MSW, and
Playwright are options rather than universal dependencies. Test observable contracts, rejected
promises, cancellation, malformed boundary data, unknown write outcomes, and cleanup. Run the
configured type checker, linter, and tests; UI code also satisfies `frontend-craft`'s real-browser and
accessibility verification.
